http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2524742-simms-long-overdue-developmental-league-would-greatly-benefit-young-players

Reading bleacher report today I saw this story that intrigued me. I would honestly love a developmental league. It would help develop talent and cater to the players that really don't want to do the schooling required by the NCAA just to play football to get ready for the next level. Plus it could potentially be a spring league, which would mean more football!
What's your take on an NFL developmental league?

The average NFL career is what? 4 years?

Why should 5 star talent choose developmental league over college scholarship (including housing, food, clothing, campus life)?

College scholarships for these guys is the real prize and we should be encouraging them to finish their degrees, not to gamble everything on their body's ability to stay healthy.

My roommate played for my University's team so I got to meet a lot of the players. One of them was just suspended because he didn't like going to class. He's 5'10 and runs a 4.6 at 195 pounds. This is the kind of guy who would play in a developmental league and then a year later is going to be selling drugs on the street corner.

Why should college ball be the only stepping stone to the NFL? Most of the top talent go just because they have to, not because they want to. A developmental league could offer these guys an alternate route at a set salary and even potentially offer an insurance policy. The 5'10 195 pounders would still be able to play for college teams, hell they would even have a better chance at playing in a major program.

A developmental league wouldn't take away scholarships, it would make more available by not using those on the ones that are only doing it because they have to. And the quality of college football wouldn't drop because the skimming of a few to roster a 16 or so team league wouldn't put much of a dent in the 128 team division I the NCAA currently has.

"We ain't come to play school" is all the reason anyone needs to see that college is a great opportunity for these guys. A developmental league will have far more failures than successes.

College ball should be the only stepping stone to the NFL because a college degree will help most of these guys far more than a D League ever will.

The college option would still be there and the D League would offer those who don't want to play school a different route. Let's face it the guys who come to play only football don't gain much from school because they don't participate in that side of it. They skip class or just don't pay attention if they are forced to go and have 'tutors' do everything for them.

I disagree wholeheartedly.

A degree is the difference between a good job and a poor one. Nearly every decent paying job requires some kind of degree. Without a degree they are going to be working dead end jobs.

It's systematic racism. The D league is a system that is based on milking the profitability of people who won't be able to gain anything from their time in the program. Money is the best motivator and the largest adopter for a D league is going to be the dumb kids from the inner city schools whom have poor funding and poor teaching.

Let's say that there are 16 teams and 32 players a team. Enough to field a team and have the best players play both ways. How many do you think will it to a training camp?

I'd say 5 tops. I'd say 0 make a roster.

Now what is the D league going to pay for such talent? Well right now NFL contracts are not guaranteed so you can be sure these won't be guaranteed either. I'd guess that these kids would be making low five figures for their stint in the D league, not including things like relocation costs or heaven forbid medical costs. Most of the NFL doesn't want to provide medical coverage for their retired players let alone some scrubs with no money and no future.

Meanwhile what is the NFL going to do? They are going to monetize. Put it on TV during the spring and make a ton of money off these players. Sell it as watching tomorrow's future stars when in reality you're just seeing guys that you're going to avoid if you ever saw them on the street.

It's a mousetrap bruh, except the NFL finally think they can broadcast it and make money off of it. This doesn't help players.

What makes you think this type of character you described is going to EARN their degree and not just have it handed to them for playing for a program for four years? I'm sure there's the exception that do take it seriously and benefit from it, but my experience on campus point out to a majority being handed a degree.

Salary wise I would say a D League would be on par with the CFL. Minimum 50k with an average of 80k. And those "dumb kids from poor schools" will have the college program available. I do agree most of them would jump to the D League and some get burned in the long run and screw their life up, but no more than the ones that go to school don't study get suspended and have their scholarships pulled and screw their life up.

And the NFL would monetize the hell out of it, I don't doubt that. The NFL is a shit company, but they have the see a monetary purpose behind something like this or it isn't feasible to a company that likes to profit.

I think rather than a developmental league, colleges and college coaches should have some incentive to give their players the best shot at succeeding in the NFL. This would, hopefully, change the direction of college football. Rather than the only focus being to win, and utilizing tactics that are proven to fail in the NFL such as the "spread offense", there is more focus on a pro-style offense and the development of their players.
It would be absolutely wonderful if this could work out, but these coaches are paid to win and that's it.

Yeah, currently that's how it works and it won't change until other incentives are provided.

But, you could - for example - give coaches and/or universities bonuses for not only every player drafted into the NFL, but only those that stay beyond their rookie deal or something. Obviously that's a very vague example, but there could be monetary incentives provided to coaches and/or universities that prod coaches to care about the success of their players beyond college, rather than just winning.
